emergency.notes: 112 handles all emergencies. Tourist hotline: 1505. Georgian emergency services have improved significantly but response times in rural mountain areas can be long.

travelAdvisory.summary: Exercise increased caution in Georgia due to the Russian-occupied regions of South Ossetia and Abkhazia. Do not travel to these occupied territories. Georgia proper is generally safe for tourists.

travelAdvisoryUK.summary: Most visits to Georgia are trouble-free. Avoid the occupied regions of South Ossetia and Abkhazia. Take care in mountain areas.

healthcare.costForTourists: Healthcare is affordable. Private clinic visit $20-60. Emergency room $100-300. Hospital stay $100-400/night. Quality varies significantly — private hospitals are better than public.
healthcare.pharmacyAccess: Pharmacies (apteka) widespread in cities. Many medications available OTC. Some English spoken in pharmacies in Tbilisi.
healthcare.hospitalNotes: Private hospitals in Tbilisi offer reasonable care. Gudushauri National Medical Center handles trauma cases. For serious conditions, consider evacuation to Turkey (Istanbul) or Germany.
vaccinationsRecommended: Rabies (if hiking or in contact with animals)
healthcare.insuranceAdvice: Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage strongly recommended. Helicopter rescue in the Caucasus mountains is expensive and may require private arrangements.
healthcare.summary: Georgia has improving healthcare with decent private clinics in Tbilisi, though facilities outside the capital are limited. For serious medical conditions, evacuation to Turkey or Western Europe may be necessary. Costs are very affordable for travelers.

vaccinations.name: Hepatitis A
vaccinations.note: Recommended for all travelers due to potential food and water exposure.

vaccinations.name: Hepatitis B
vaccinations.note: Recommended for travelers who may have medical treatment or intimate contact.

vaccinations.name: Typhoid
vaccinations.note: Consider if eating from street vendors or visiting rural areas.

vaccinations.name: Rabies
vaccinations.note: Consider for hikers and those with potential animal contact in rural/mountain areas.

vaccinations.name: Routine vaccinations
vaccinations.note: Ensure routine vaccinations (MMR, DPT, polio, flu) are up to date.

risks.name: Waterborne illness
risks.note: Tap water quality varies. Stick to bottled water outside Tbilisi.

risks.name: Mountain hazards
risks.note: Hiking in the Caucasus carries risks of altitude, weather changes, and limited rescue services.

risks.name: Tick-borne diseases
risks.note: Risk of tick-borne encephalitis in forested areas during spring and summer.

risks.name: Rabies
risks.note: Stray dogs are common in cities and rural areas. Avoid contact with strays.

controlledSubstances.note: Carry original prescription and doctor's letter. Keep in original packaging. Georgia has historically been strict on drugs — verify current regulations before travel.
Possession of cannabis for personal use was decriminalized in 2018 but sales remain illegal. Do not bring cannabis products into Georgia.

medications.generalAdvice: Georgia has relaxed some drug laws but remains conservative about controlled substances. Carry all prescription medications in original packaging with documentation. Import of narcotics requires advance approval.

scams.name: Fake currency exchange
scams.description: Street money changers offer better exchange rates but give you outdated or fake currency. Short-changing is also common.
scams.avoidance: Use official exchange offices (saqalaqo) or ATMs. Never exchange money on the street. Check your bills carefully.

scams.name: Overly friendly taxi drivers
scams.description: Taxi drivers take tourists to shops, restaurants, or guesthouses where they receive commission. Fares can also be inflated for tourists.
scams.avoidance: Use Yandex.Taxi or Bolt ride-hailing apps for transparent pricing. Agree on price before getting in unmarked taxis.

connectivity.simOptions: SIM cards from Magti, Geocell (Silknet), or Beeline available at airports and convenience stores. ~GEL 15-30 ($6-12) for tourist packages with 5-20GB. eSIM via Airalo.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi widely available in Tbilisi cafes, restaurants, and hotels. Mountain resort towns have reasonable WiFi. Rural areas have limited connectivity.
connectivity.bestOption: Magti SIM for best coverage including mountain areas. Available at Tbilisi airport.

cultural.tipping: Tipping is not traditional but is becoming expected in tourist-facing businesses. Restaurants: 10% is generous. Taxi: round up. Traditional Georgian hospitality (supra feast) — no tipping expected at family homes.
cultural.dressCode: Modest dress is respected. Cover shoulders and knees at churches. Women should cover their hair in Orthodox churches (scarves available at entrances). Georgians dress up for evenings out.
cultural.greetings: Men shake hands. Women often exchange cheek kisses. 'Gamarjoba' (hello) is always appreciated. Georgians are extremely hospitable — be prepared for insistent offers of food and wine.
taboos: Refusing food or wine at a Georgian supra (feast) is considered impolite
Disrespecting Orthodox churches or religious symbols
Taking photos inside churches without asking
Wasting food when a host has cooked for you
cultural.haggling: Some negotiation is possible at markets. Prices in restaurants and shops are generally fixed.

safety.lgbtSafety: LGBTQ+ rights are limited. Same-sex relationships are legal but not recognized. LGBTQ+ individuals face societal discrimination and hostility, particularly from religious groups. In 2023, far-right groups disrupted Tbilisi Pride. Exercise significant discretion.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Generally safe. Georgian men can be assertive but rarely aggressive with Western women. Exercise caution at night in less-touristed areas.
safety.notes: Georgia is generally very safe for tourists. Do not enter the occupied territories of South Ossetia or Abkhazia. The areas near the administrative boundary lines are unpredictable. Tbilisi's old city is very tourist-friendly. Hiking in the Caucasus requires preparation and local guides.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: 365 days visa-free (one of the most generous in the world). UK, EU: 1 year visa-free. Many nationalities get 1-year entry without a visa.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: May-June and September-October for hiking and mild weather. December-March for skiing in Gudauri. Avoid July-August (hot, crowded in Tbilisi).
